title: GSK vs. SNY: Which Europe-Based Pharma Stock Has More Potential?
author: Na
description: GSK and Sanofi, two major European pharmaceutical companies, are compared across growth drivers, pipelines, and valuations. GSK shows strong specialty medicines growth (14% in H1 2026) with expanding oncology and HIV franchises, while Sanofi benefits from blockbuster Dupixent sales (up 28.6%) and stronger near-term earnings growth. Despite both holding Hold ratings, Sanofi appears better positioned due to superior earnings growth outlook, favorable valuation metrics, and positive estimate revisions, though it faces vaccine sales headwinds and heavy Dupixent reliance.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: GSK demonstrates solid specialty medicines growth (14% in H1 2026) and expanding pipeline with multiple late-stage programs. However, it faces patent expirations for key HIV drugs (2028-2029), declining general medicines segment, and recent pipeline setbacks. Earnings estimates have declined over the past 60 days, and stock performance lags the industry.

Sanofi shows stronger near-term growth with 13.9% sales growth and 14.5% EPS growth expected for 2026. Dupixent sales surged 28.6% with €25 billion projected by 2030. Earnings estimates have risen over 60 days, valuation is more attractive (7.87 forward P/E vs industry 18.23), and dividend yield is higher at 4.3%. Management raised full-year guidance based on strong H1 performance.

Regeneron is mentioned as the partner in Sanofi's blockbuster Dupixent drug, which is performing exceptionally well. However, the article provides limited direct information about Regeneron's independent performance or outlook.

title: HUTCHMED Initiates Global Trial of KRAS-EGFR-Antibody Conjugate Therapy HMPL-A830 in Patients with Solid Tumors
author: Hutchmed (China) Limited
description: HUTCHMED has initiated a Phase Ia global clinical trial of HMPL-A830, a first-in-class antibody-targeted therapy conjugate combining a KRAS inhibitor with an anti-EGFR antibody for treating solid tumors. The first patient was dosed on September 24, 2026. HUTCHMED entered an exclusive development and licensing agreement with GSK on September 3, 2026, granting GSK worldwide rights (excluding Greater China) for development and commercialization.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Company successfully initiated a first-in-class clinical trial for an innovative dual-mechanism cancer therapy and secured a major global licensing partnership with GSK, demonstrating validation of its ATTC platform and expanding market reach beyond China.

GSK acquired exclusive worldwide rights (excluding Greater China) to develop and commercialize a first-in-class KRAS-EGFR therapy, providing access to a promising oncology asset addressing significant clinical gaps in KRAS-mutant cancers.

title: Autoimmune Disease Therapeutics Market Set for Growth Through 2034 as Biologics, Precision Medicine and Pipeline Innovation Reshape the Competitive Landscape
author: Researchandmarkets.Com
description: The global autoimmune disease therapeutics market is projected to grow from USD 132.75 billion in 2025 to USD 254.60 billion by 2034, at a CAGR of 7.5%. Growth is driven by rising autoimmune disease diagnoses, increased adoption of biologics and targeted oral therapies, biosimilar expansion, and emerging cell and gene therapies. Biologics dominate with 66% market share, TNF inhibitors lead drug classes at 29%, and rheumatoid arthritis accounts for 34% of revenue. North America holds 44% regional share while Asia-Pacific is expected to grow fastest.

title: Hypertension Clinical Trial Pipeline Accelerates as 100+ Pharma Companies Rigorously Develop Drugs for Market Entry | DelveInsight
author: Delveinsight
description: Over 100 pharmaceutical companies are actively developing 110+ pipeline hypertension drugs, with approximately 40+ in late-stage development. Key players include Gossamer Bio, Alnylam Therapeutics, Roche, GSK, and others pursuing novel mechanisms like RNA interference and CRAC channel inhibitors. Recent developments include FDA acceptance of lorundrostat's NDA, initiation of zilebesiran's Phase III cardiovascular outcomes trial, and multiple clinical advances in emerging therapies targeting uncontrolled and resistant hypertension.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Company secured $250 million in private placement financing for seralutinib development in PAH and PH-ILD, with planned NDA submission in September 2026, indicating strong investor confidence and advancement toward market entry.
Partnered with Alnylam on zilebesiran Phase III trial and reacquired worldwide rights to seralutinib, demonstrating commitment to expanding hypertension pipeline with innovative mechanisms.
Acquired 35Pharma Inc. including HS235 candidate for PAH and PH-HFpEF, expanding pipeline with novel protein-based therapeutics for hypertension-related conditions.
Advancing CM5480, a first-in-class oral CRAC channel inhibitor with IND submission anticipated in 2027, targeting pulmonary vascular remodeling in pulmonary hypertension.

Lorundrostat received FDA NDA acceptance with PDUFA target date of December 22, 2026, and demonstrated significant efficacy in Phase III trials for uncontrolled/resistant hypertension, positioning it as a leading novel conventional antihypertensive.
CTX340 targeting angiotensinogen received FDA IND clearance with Phase I trial initiated for refractory hypertension, representing progress in gene-editing approach to hypertension treatment.

Tonlamarsen (ASO targeting angiotensinogen) demonstrated statistically significant reduction in plasma AGT levels and clinically meaningful blood pressure reduction in Phase II KARDINAL trial, supporting advancement to Phase IIb.

title: Managing Service Providers Including CRO and CMOs Oversight to Comply with ICH GCP R3 Scheduled for October 14–15, 2027
author: Not Specified
description: A two-day online training course on managing Contract Research Organisations (CROs) and Contract Manufacturing Organisations (CMOs) under ICH GCP R3 guidelines will be delivered by IPI Academy on October 14-15, 2027.
